6. SO -> (GH v H)
7. EI -> C
8. FF -> SO
9. VF v EI
10. IP XOR VF
11. AN -> FF
12. IP -> FF
13. AN v PP

- Since we know S is true (2), for (S XOR H) to be true, H must be false. So, ~H (Max is not happy).
- From (7) EI -> C and (4) ~C, by Modus Tollens, we get ~EI (Max does not enjoy independence).
- From (9) VF v EI and ~EI, by Disjunctive Syllogism, we get VF (Max values freedom).
- From (10) IP XOR VF and VF, for the exclusive disjunction to be true, IP must be false. So, ~IP (Max does not find inner peace).
- From (6) SO -> (GH v H), we know ~GH (3) and ~H (derived above). This means (GH v H) is false. By Modus Tollens, we get ~SO (Max does not smile often).
- From (8) FF -> SO and ~SO, by Modus Tollens, we get ~FF (Max does not feel fulfilled).
- From (11) AN -> FF and ~FF, by Modus Tollens, we get ~AN (Max does not appreciate nature).
- Finally, from (13) AN v PP and ~AN, by Disjunctive Syllogism, we must conclude PP (Max pursues his passion).
